retained_exact_results: Typed Hall allocation is exact only after concrete missing B-edge carriers and graph-proved legal arcs have been constructed.
In a locked d-demand circuit with common two-point support and common reserve K(e), matching rank is min(d,|K(e)|), and any saturation needs at least d-|K(e)| distinct external actual carriers.
The n=14 threshold graph is rainbow-C7 and L4(2), has four locked demands and K(bc)={bc,cz}, hence carrier rank two and deficiency two.
not_inherited: No actual absorber, external legal arc, codegree theorem, nibble cleanup, or 1/8 implication is inherited.
Round-four mechanisms M809R4-02 and M809R4-05 were not strictly refuted after audit and are not promoted as theorems.

absorber_type_firewall.demand: A concrete repeated-colour defect with its labelled original-graph endpoints, chosen root, base e and canonical reserve K(e).
absorber_type_firewall.external_output: A concrete missing B-edge f in the same original graph with f not in K(e) before the switch.
absorber_type_firewall.legal_arc: A replayable original-graph operation proving that this named demand may use f; membership of f in the global missing-edge set or appearance in an abstract catalogue is insufficient.
absorber_type_firewall.certificate: The demand, original base and reserve, complete switch gadget, output f, all C7 witnesses, and ownership resources used by the switch.
absorber_type_firewall.output_rank: Maximum number of demands assigned distinct output B-edges by pairwise compatible certificates; certificate multiplicity is not rank.
absorber_type_firewall.cut_expansion: For every demand cut T, the union of old canonical neighbours and legal external outputs has size at least |T| after occupied outputs and ownership conflicts are removed.

inherited_methods.loss_step: Count graph paths, C7 witnesses, root labels or source rectangles as separate absorbers before projecting to named output missing B-edges.
inherited_methods.lost_information: Many certificates may share one output or one indispensable witness, so their compatible matching rank can remain one.
inherited_methods.exact_witness: The locked n=14 graph already has many graph paths and cycle witnesses but only two actual outputs in K(bc); witness multiplicity cannot exceed output rank two.
inherited_methods.consequence: Every count must be accompanied by maximum output codegree and ownership-codegree bounds.

inherited_methods.loss_step: Use large common neighbourhoods of local witnesses as though they contained many distinct external missing B-edges.
inherited_methods.lost_information: DRC preserves common witness multiplicity but can concentrate all witnesses on the same output fibre.
inherited_methods.exact_witness: All locked demands have identical canonical neighbourhood {bc,cz}; arbitrary multiplicity of source witnesses leaves the same two-edge image.
inherited_methods.consequence: DRC must be applied after the output projection or prove a bound on every projected fibre.

inherited_methods.loss_step: Take certificate degree as the hypergraph vertex degree without retaining pair codegrees on output edges and switch resources.
inherited_methods.lost_information: A large multi-hypergraph of certificates can have pair codegree equal to degree and matching number one.
inherited_methods.exact_witness: The n=14 identical-base class has demand pair codegree equal to individual output degree.
inherited_methods.consequence: A nibble needs graph-derived output and resource codegrees plus deterministic all-cut cleanup.

inherited_methods.loss_step: Declare switch certificates independent or linkable before proving that exchange paths preserve their concrete B-edge outputs and C7 legality.
inherited_methods.lost_information: The exchange may end at an old reserve edge, reuse one output, or change only an A-side owner.
inherited_methods.exact_witness: Four distinct owned A diagonals coexist with B-output rank two in the locked graph.
inherited_methods.consequence: Any parity/linkage theorem must use a common ground set of actual missing B-edges and replay every exchange.

inherited_methods.method: stability decomposition into typical and exceptional vertices
inherited_methods.loss_step: Discard a small exceptional set before verifying which vertices carry all external absorber outputs.
inherited_methods.lost_information: All rank-increasing outputs may be concentrated on the exceptional set, while the typical graph has a huge but rank-neutral catalogue.
inherited_methods.consequence: The decomposition must preserve each deficient cut's output neighbourhood and codegree ledger.

required_new_information: An explicit local switch in the original hard graph that takes a named demand to a missing B-edge outside its original K(e).
A proof that the switch is C7-legal and retains all required hard-branch hypotheses.
A bounded-overlap theorem for both output B-edges and every internal switch resource.
A matching or linkage theorem whose conclusion is expansion for every demand cut, not merely many certificates or large expected matching.
Composition with the outer-A gate and all public hard branches before any 1/8 claim.
forbidden_shortcut: Abstract dummies, conditional Hall, path multiplicity, certificates lacking an external output, and finite absence of a blocker are not actual-absorber progress.
